title: What do we get when we keep adding the next number?
description: The numbers three, six, nine and twelve are added up one at a time, and the total after each step is written down. Each total holds all the numbers so far. Keeko doubts this and says the totals are the same list again.
teaching_notes: One idea: a running total is the last total plus the next number, so each total holds every number so far. Watch for students who write the sequence itself instead of the totals.

source: Find the running totals of the sequence 3, 6, 9, 12.
video_script.why: The child learns to build running totals by adding the next number to the total so far, the way the book adds up odd numbers.
video_script.substitution: The book adds up the odd numbers; here the numbers are three, six, nine and twelve.
video_script.anchor: four numbers in a row with a growing total written under each
video_script.wrong_answer: the running totals are three, six, nine and twelve again
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the running totals are three, six, nine and twelve again. The second total holds the first and second numbers together, so it is more than six, and the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The running totals are three, nine, eighteen and thirty
maths_rules: slip: 3, 6, 9, 12 is the sequence itself, not its totals; the second total 9 is more than 6
video_script.design: Four numbers sit in a row. A total is built under each, one step at a time, with the last total carried forward and the next number added to it.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the numbers 3, 6, 9, 12 in a row, with an empty box under each

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.nums: the four numbers appear in a row with empty boxes under them
marks.ask: a question mark appears over the empty boxes

beats.colours: numbers in blue, empty boxes outlined
narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about adding up numbers one step at a time.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>The numbers are three, six, nine and twelve.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We add the first number, then the first two, then the first three, and then all four. What totals do we get?

beats.on_screen: the numbers and empty boxes stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the numbers 3, 6, 9, 12 labelled sequence; a bracket around the first two numbers labelled running total

marks.seq: the label sequence appears under the four numbers
marks.total: a bracket closes round the first numbers and a total box fills
marks.run: the label running total appears on the box

narration: <bookmark mark='seq'/>Numbers in a fixed order, like these four, are called a sequence.
<bookmark mark='total'/>Adding up the numbers one at a time gives a total after each step.
<bookmark mark='run'/>These totals are called running totals.

marks.given: the sequence is written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the sequence three, six, nine and twelve.
<bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the running totals of this sequence.

marks.first: the first number, 3, drops into the first total box

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, the first total is the first number alone, because nothing has been added to it yet. That is three.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: total so far + next number = 3 + 6 = 9

marks.add: the total 3 and the next number 6 join with a plus sign

beats.colours: total so far in gold, next number in blue
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, add the next number to the total so far. Each total holds every number up to now.
<bookmark mark='make'/>Three plus six gives nine.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: total so far + next number = 9 + 9 = 18

marks.add: the total 9 and the next number 9 join with a plus sign

beats.colours: total so far in gold, next number in blue
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add the next number to the total so far again. The total is nine and the next number is nine.
<bookmark mark='make'/>Nine plus nine gives eighteen.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: total so far + next number = 18 + 12 = 30

marks.add: the total 18 and the last number 12 join with a plus sign

beats.colours: total so far in gold, next number in blue
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step four, add the last number to the total so far. The total is eighteen and the last number is twelve.
<bookmark mark='make'/>Eighteen plus twelve gives thirty.

marks.ans: the four totals are boxed in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The running totals are three, nine, eighteen and thirty. Each one is the last total plus the next number.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says 3, 6, 9, 12; the first two numbers 3 and 6 are pushed together into one pile of 9; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.pile: the numbers 3 and 6 are pushed together into one pile

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the running totals are three, six, nine and twelve again.
<bookmark mark='pile'/>After the second step, the total holds the first and second numbers together.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>That pile is more than six, so the totals cannot be the same list as the sequence.
